title: Chemical revolution
summary: The English Wikipedia article "Chemical revolution", at revision 1376541983, opens: "In the history of chemistry, the chemical revolution, also called the first chemical revolution, was the reformulation of chemistry during the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, which culminated in the law of conservation of mass and the oxygen theory of combustion." That is the article's account and not yet this atlas's; nobody has read this record, and review.html is where somebody does. Wikidata item Q1340216, imported by tools/import/wikidata.mjs. The item's own description reads "early modern reformulation of chemistry that culminated in the law of conservation of mass and the oxygen theory of combustion". Everything here is copied from the item's own fields and nothing in it is this atlas's account of the thing: that is still to be written, and review.html is where somebody writes it.
